baseline.audited: Audit of 2026-07-30 (SPRINT.md § Where the engine actually is today); rows re-pulled verbatim from the memories collection 2026-07-31.

final_brief.problem: Group camping trips have no shared system — the organizer manually herds gear lists, meal plans, and cost-splitting across texts and spreadsheets, while the whole group suffers the fallout of forgotten gear and unresolved money disputes.
final_brief.who: Draft: recurring trip organizers — friends or family members who plan group camping trips (3+ people) more than once a year and currently coordinate via texts, spreadsheets, and Splitwise.
final_brief.value: A single shared system that guarantees nobody forgets gear and money never turns into a post-trip fight — for every group trip, big or small.

rows.content: Both the organizer and the wider group feel the pain — organizer does the planning work, group suffers the resulting chaos.
rows.verbatim: Both — organizer plans, group feels the mess

rows.content: Founder confirmed the problem statement: organizer manually herds logistics while the whole group suffers the fallout.
The coordination chaos hits every trip, even small ones, not just big trips.
Core value is twofold: eliminating forgotten gear and eliminating unresolved cost-splitting disputes, equally.
Founder decided to ship both the gear checklist and cost-split tracker as day-one features, not sequenced.
Groups currently cope via multiple text threads and phone calls, which leads to arguments and something always missing.
rows.verbatim: basically texts (mulitple of them) and phone calls and fights and always something is missing

rows.content: The cost of the chaos is wasted time, one person unfairly bearing money-chasing burden, and it souring the whole trip experience.
rows.verbatim: wasted time+ unfair for one person sometimes losing money or having to keep following up on money  pretty much the whole experince

rows.content: Founder believes groups don't know a better way exists and no one has built a tool for this specific recurring group-camping use case.
rows.verbatim: groups do not know anything better and i dont think anyone has built suuch a thing

rows.content: Founder envisions an AI onboarding flow: host answers questions, AI auto-generates a shared gear board.
